newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Eurostat sets effect of Italian eurotax lower.
newsitem.headline: Eurostat sets effect of Italian eurotax lower.

text.p: Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, decision on Friday on Italy's 1997 deficit plan includes less than the European Commission incorporated into its prior outlook.
Regarding the treatment of the part of the so-called eurotax in dispute, Eurostat approved 3.5 trillion lire ($2.1 billion), about 0.2 percent of GDP.
The Commission's November estimate of Italy's 1997 budget deficit assumed a much larger 0.6-percent of GDP, a Commission official said.
Commission officials said the remaining portion of the tax that was about 0.4 percent of GDP was not under dispute in this latest review.
Regarding the treatment of state guarantees for Italy's railways system, Eurostat also approved a smaller 0.2-percent of GDP versus the Commission's 0.3-percent assumption.

Commission officials warned, however, that one should not extrapolate any judgments on Italy's 1997 deficit outlook from Eurostat's ruling. Many factors, particularly Italy's economic situation, will be taken into account in April when the Commission issues revised forecasts for the deficits in each of the 15 EU states.
